artworks.title: Frontispiece for "Balli di Sfessania"
artworks.medium: etching and engraving on laid paper
artworks.description: This is a drawing of three costumed figures in a theatrical scene. The characters are wearing masks with exaggerated features, typical of commedia dell'arte. The figure on the left is playing a stringed instrument, the central figure is playing a tambourine and moving energetically, and the figure on the right is holding an accordion-like instrument. Additional heads are peeking out from behind curtains. The title "Balli di Sfessania" is written on the image. The drawing style shows early Baroque influence.

artworks.title: Guatsetto and Mestolino
artworks.description: This is a drawing of two large, masked figures with feathered hats facing each other amidst a scene with smaller figures also in feathered attire. The two central figures on either side of the composition are clothed in long robes and wear large brimmed hats adorned with long feathers. Each holds a long, thin sword or similar object. In the background, a scene full of lively smaller figures, possibly engaging in dance or procession, is depicted, creating an energetic atmosphere. These smaller figures wear elaborate costumes with feathers, some holding instruments or gesturing animatedly. The composition is marked by its exaggerated and whimsical style. The notable use of line and shading gives depth and texture to the figures and setting.

artworks.title: Cucorongna and Pernoualla
artworks.description: This is a drawing of two fantastical figures engaged in an animated stance. The drawing features two detailed figures with exaggerated postures and peculiar facial expressions. They are adorned with large hats topped with feathers and appear to be engaging with each other. The figure on the left is labeled "Cucorongna," while the one on the right is labeled "Pernoualla." Each figure has a dynamic pose, highlighting movement and drama. In the background, there are smaller figures observing or participating in a similar activity. The landscape includes distant structures. The drawing is executed in a monochrome palette.

artworks.title: Cicho Sgarra and Collo Francisco
artworks.description: This is an illustration of two fantastical creatures in dynamic poses, with a crowd of smaller figures in the background. The creatures are labeled "Cicho Sgarra" and "Collo Francisco" and appear as anthropomorphic figures with exaggerated muscular forms and elongated features. They have distinctive beak-like protrusions on their faces and large feathers or plumes on their heads. The creatures are shown in mid-stride with arms raised or extended, suggesting motion. In the background, there is a group of smaller figures in various poses and attire, likely human. The illustration features fine linework and detailed patterns and textures.

artworks.title: Cap. Cerimonia and Siga. Lavinia
artworks.description: This is a drawing of two figures standing in a town setting. The left figure is a creature with a hulking form, avian mask, bat-like wings, and long robes. The right figure is a tall, elegant person in a dress with a feathered hat. The background shows small figures engaged in various activities in a town square. The figures are labelled as "Cap. Cerimonia" and "Sig.ra Lauinia."

artworks.title: Gian Fritello and Ciurlo
artworks.description: This is an image featuring two fantastical figures. One figure, labeled "Gian Frittello," is tall and thin with elongated limbs, while the other, labeled "Ciurlo," is muscular and energetic. Both figures are depicted wielding swords in expressive poses. The drawing includes intricate details in the costumes and background elements like smaller figures in various activities.

artworks.title: Smaralo Cornuto and Ratsa di Boio
artworks.description: This is a drawing of two large, exaggerated figures in a surreal landscape. One figure has a long nose, a cape with fringes, and a scrawny build, while the other is muscular with outstretched arms and a large head with striped patterns. In the background, there are people dancing around two tall, stick-like figures. The setting includes scattered architectural structures suggesting a village or town, with simple buildings and towers. The style is linear and detailed, resembling 17th-century European prints, with absurd and fantastical elements.

artworks.title: Riciulina and Metzetin
artworks.description: The image features two characters, Riculina and Metzetin, depicted in full body views. Riculina is on the left, standing with one leg raised and arms bent in a gesture. She has distinct facial features, curly hair tied up with a bow and feathers, and wears a detailed costume with a beaded necklace. Metzetin is on the right, holding a large stringed instrument and wearing a pointed hat with a plume, a flowing coat, and tied trousers. The background shows a gathering of people and buildings, framed by trees.

artworks.title: Fracischina and Gian Farina
artworks.description: This is a drawing of an animated dance scene. The image depicts two figures at the center, one holding a tambourine overhead, and the other wielding a sword while seemingly in mid-dance. Both figures are dressed in flowing garments. In the background, a group of smaller figures are engaged in various forms of activity. The scene is set in what appears to be a town square, indicated by the architectural outlines of buildings in the distance.

artworks.title: Signa. Lucia and Trastullo
artworks.description: This image shows a detailed drawing of two figures. On the left, a woman stands in profile with her body slightly turned towards a kneeling man on the right. The woman has an updo adorned with a decorative piece, wearing a long dress, while the man has long hair and is dressed in loose-fitting clothing. The background depicts a city square with buildings on either side, and there are smaller figures visible in the background. The text at the bottom reads "Sig.a Lucia. Trastullo."

artworks.title: Bello Sguardo and Coviello
artworks.description: This is a drawing of two fantastical figures dancing. The two figures have elongated limbs and exaggerated anatomical features. Each figure is draped with a flowing, tattered garment that moves dramatically as they dance. Their poses are lively and dynamic. Both figures hold swords, and they appear to be engaged in a playful or ceremonial dance. In the background, smaller figures are gathered, possibly watching the main subjects. Some structures and a few bare trees are visible. The drawing is monochromatic, executed in black ink on paper.

artworks.title: Cap. Cardoni and Maramao
artworks.description: The image shows an illustration featuring two full-body figures engaged in a humorous duel. The person on the left is labeled "Cap. Cardoni." This figure stands with a hunched posture, leaning back with one foot forward and one arm raised behind the head. The person has exaggerated facial features with a long nose and wild, flowing hair. They are wearing a stylized outfit with large sleeves and an ornate collar. The person on the right is labeled "Maramao." This individual is in a dynamic stance, leaning forward with a long staff in hand aimed towards the other person's midsection. This person also has an exaggerated nose and is wearing a hat with feathers. Their clothing is ornate, with puffed sleeves and decorative patterns. In the background, several figures are visible in a town setting with buildings and a group of people. The setting suggests a lively and bustling atmosphere with an emphasis on theatrical elements.

artworks.title: Razullo and Cucurucu
artworks.description: This is a drawing of two costumed figures performing in a town square. The drawing depicts two figures labeled "Razullo" and "Cucurucu" engaged in a theatrical performance. "Razullo" is on the left, wearing a costume with large buttons and holding a long necked-stringed instrument. "Cucurucu" is on the right, shown in a similarly expressive pose with one arm raised. Both figures wear hats with feathers. The background shows townspeople gathered around a raised platform, with buildings enclosing the square. The image is detailed with fine lines, capturing the theatrical scene.

artworks.title: Franca Trippa and Fritellino
artworks.description: This is a drawing of two costumed figures labeled "Franca Trippa" and "Fritellino." The drawing shows two individuals dressed in theatrical costumes, each captured in a dynamic pose. Both figures are depicted with exaggerated costumes and hats. The figure on the left holds a spoon and wears an apron, while the figure on the right holds a stringed instrument. In the background, there are several buildings and a group of characters engaged in various activities, suggesting a street scene. The style of this drawing shows intricate line work and attention to costumes and expressions.

artworks.title: Pasquariello Truonno and Meo Squaquara
artworks.description: This is a drawing of two fantastical figures with exaggerated features. The figures are depicted with elongated limbs and elaborate costumes adorned with buttons and flowing scarves, and each holds a sword. Their faces have exaggerated features such as long noses and protruding eyes. In the background, there is a scene with smaller figures possibly engaged in some form of festivity or display, with architecture and trees as part of the landscape. The image is characterized by its use of fine lines and shading to create the figures and background scenery.

artworks.title: Taglia Cantoni and Fracasso
artworks.description: This is a drawing of two figures engaged in a fencing duel. The image shows two individuals facing each other with swords drawn. Both figures are wearing period attire and are adorned with feathered hats. The stance of each figure captures movement as they prepare to engage in swordplay. In the background, smaller figures are observing or engaging in leisurely activities. The ground is lightly sketched with minimal details of a distant landscape. The drawing focuses on the energy and intensity of the duel, with exaggerated costumes and poses. The text "Taglia Cantoni" and "Fracasso" are inscribed below the figures.

artworks.title: Pulliciniello and Siga. Lucretia
artworks.description: There are two full-bodied figures in the image, a man and a woman, standing side by side facing forward. The man is labeled "Pulliciniello" on the left and poses with a slight twist to his body, holding a stick-like object under his arm. He has a large hooked nose, a mustache, and wears a loose-fitting outfit with a cape draped over one shoulder and wide-legged trousers. The woman, labeled "Sig.ra Lucretia," stands to the right holding a fan in one hand while her other hand rests on her hip. She has her hair styled up, adorned with some decoration, and wears a long, voluminous dress with gathered sleeves accentuating her waist. In the background, there are various buildings and figures engaged in what seems to be animated interactions, including dancing with raised hands and outstretched legs. The setting appears to be outdoors, resembling a village or town square.

artworks.title: Cap. Bonbardon and Cap. Grillo
artworks.description: This is a drawing of two fantastical figures in elaborate costumes posed dynamically against a backdrop of spectators. The scene features two characters titled "Cap. Bonbardon" and "Cap. Grillo" in theatrical postures. The figures are depicted with exaggerated features and wear detailed costumes, including elongated noses and feathered hats. In the background, a crowd watches the figures, emphasizing a sense of performance or public event. The intricate line work and style suggest a vivid and energetic narrative captured in an illustrative manner.

artworks.title: Cap. Spessa Monti and Bagattino
artworks.description: The image shows two full-body figures dressed in elaborate costumes. The figure on the left is labeled "Cap. Spessa Monti," standing in a dynamic posture with slightly bent knees, holding a sword and with an elongated nose, framed by a large headdress. The figure’s outfit consists of a textured garment with exaggerated drapery. The figure on the right is labeled "BaGattino," bending forward slightly, with large, mask-like facial features and an elaborate headdress. This figure also wears loose-fitting clothing. The background depicts a town scene with groups of smaller figures and ornate buildings.

artworks.title: Cap. Esgangarato and Cap. Cocodrillo
artworks.description: This is an image of two fantastical figures engaged in a dance. The drawing shows two muscular creatures with elongated limbs, wearing costumes including masks, feathered headpieces, and flowing cloth elements. They are depicted in dynamic poses, capturing motion and drama. The figures are labeled "Cap: Cgangarato" and "Cap: Cocodrillo." In the background are smaller figures in various poses, potentially part of an audience or similar event, some holding sticks or weapons. Architectural elements suggest an outdoor setting. The focus is on the physicality and theatricality of the characters in a stylized, almost mythical atmosphere.

artworks.title: Scaramucia and Fricasso
artworks.description: This is a drawing of two costumed figures engaged in a mock combat. The image shows two elaborately dressed figures with plumed hats and large capes, each brandishing a sword, as they face off in a lively duel. The environment appears to be either a stage or a public square with onlookers in the background. The scene is likely part of a theatrical performance or a festive street scene. The figures are labeled 'Scaramucia' and 'Fricasso.' In the background, additional figures watch the action. The attention to drapery and movement suggests a dynamic interaction between the figures.

artworks.title: Cap. Mala Gamba and Cap. Bellavita
artworks.description: This is a drawing of two fancifully dressed figures with exaggerated features. The left figure is labeled "Cap. Mala Gamba," posing with one arm raised and the other hand on a cloak, wearing a plumed hat. The right figure, labeled "Cap. Bellauita," strikes a similar pose with cloak and plumed hat. Both characters have large, dramatic features and exaggerated clothing typical of caricature. In the background, a group of smaller figures engage in various activities. The style suggests a playful or satirical take on military or regal personas.

artworks.title: Scapino and Cap. Zerbino
artworks.description: The image shows two full-body figures in dynamic poses. The person on the left, labeled as "Scapino," is slightly bent forward with one hand extended and the other held close to their chin. The person on the right, labeled as "Cap. Zerbino," appears to be gesturing with one hand while the other is held closer to their body. Both figures wear theatrical masks that obscure their facial features and have elaborate feathered headpieces. Their hair is not visible due to the headwear. "Scapino" wears a long, flowing robe with stripes and a belt, while "Cap. Zerbino" is dressed in form-fitting clothing with a row of buttons down the front and has a sword at their side. They are on a stage with a large jug on the ground between them. In the background, there are small figures engaged in various activities, buildings to the left, and a windblown tree to the right, suggesting a lively outdoor setting.

artworks.title: Cap. Babeo and Cucuba
artworks.description: This is a drawing of two fantastical figures in a street scene. The image features two characters labeled "Cap. Babeo" and "Cucuba" in the foreground. Both figures have exaggerated physical features and are adorned with feathered hats. Their postures suggest a confrontation or a dance. In the background, there is a scene of a bustling street with buildings and smaller figures engaged in various activities. The style of the drawing suggests an etching technique, with detailed line work capturing both the figures and the lively street setting.
